title: ExamCell
body:
Examination Management System
Project defense
Academic planning, exam operations and controlled result publication
notes: Opening: “ExamCell is a web application that helps an examination cell manage the examination lifecycle. Administrators organize exams and approve publication, teachers submit assigned marks, and students access their own published records.” Introduce yourself, institution, supervisor and team verbally. Suggested pacing: a selected main route in about 10–11 minutes, a 3–4 minute demo and 3–5 minutes for questions. See the companion guide for the recommended slide selection. Slides 21 onward are technical backup.

title: Problem and project objectives
body:
Scattered records make exam coordination difficult
Timetables must respect students and room capacity
Marks need completeness checks and approval
Students need a clear source for schedules and results
notes: Explain the problem as the project motivation, not a measured study of a particular university. The design aims to centralize records, prevent invalid transitions and improve access to published information. No measured time savings or error reduction have been established in this review.

title: System scope
body:
Academic setup and role accounts
Date sheets, seating and invigilation
Admit cards with QR verification
Marks, grading, results and rechecking
Reports, audit records, backups and optional AI
notes: This is an examination administration system. It does not implement an online exam-taking engine or automatic answer evaluation. Mention the connected workflow rather than listing every screen.

title: Users and permissions
body:
Administrator: setup, scheduling, approvals and settings
Teacher: assigned courses, marks and invigilation duties
Student: own schedules, seats, admit cards and published results
notes: Role middleware controls entry to role routes. Policies and scoped database queries also check ownership or teaching assignments. An active signed-in account is required for protected workflows. Public admit verification is a narrowly exposed exception.

title: Administrator workspace
body: A central workspace for examination operations
notes: This is a repository-provided product screenshot, not a live deployment capture. The shown counts and dates are demonstration data, not project evaluation results. Explain the navigation and how academic records feed examination operations.

title: Technology and architecture
body:
Browser: Blade, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js and Chart.js
Server: PHP 8.2+ and Laravel 12
Application: controllers, policies and domain services
Data: MySQL through Eloquent models
Background work: database queue and scheduler
notes: Architecture: a server-rendered Laravel monolith, with MVC organization and a service layer for business rules. Browser requests pass through routes and middleware to controllers. Controllers authorize and validate inputs, services run domain operations, and models persist records. DomPDF creates PDFs. Endroid creates QR codes. Vite builds frontend assets. Package manifests declare versions, but this review did not validate the installed runtime.

title: Academic setup
body:
Sessions contain semesters
Departments and semesters define sections
Students enroll in courses and sections
Teachers receive course and section assignments
Approved grading rules support examinations
notes: Setup order matters. Create the academic structure and users before trying to schedule exams or submit marks. An examination course links an examination to a course and section. Components define the scoring structure for that paper. Explain why course and exam_course are separate: one course can appear in many examination instances.

title: Examination lifecycle
body:
1. Create a draft examination and papers
2. Prepare the timetable, seats and duties
3. Approve the examination
4. Publish after operational checks
5. Create a revision when the published plan changes
notes: The implemented exam transitions are draft to approved to published. Publishing a revision archives the previous published examination. Publication checks include an approved grading scheme, component weights totaling 100%, scheduled courses, eligible seating and primary invigilation coverage. Existing published plans are protected from direct seating edits.

title: Timetable generation and conflicts
body:
Checks session dates and paper duration
Rejects overlapping papers for shared students
Checks active rooms, capacity and room unavailability
Supports multiple rooms and shared start-time slots
Rolls back generation when a paper has no valid slot
notes: The baseline generator is greedy. It visits exam courses by ID, scans days at 09:00, 13:00 and 17:00, and considers active rooms by descending capacity. It accepts the first feasible allocation. It is not a proof of globally optimal scheduling. Shared rooms are permitted for papers starting together, subject to combined capacity and separate seats. AI date-sheet validation adds checks such as teacher clashes and interpreted scheduling constraints.

title: Seating and room layouts
body:
Every eligible student needs one valid seat
Seat numbers must fit the allocated room capacity
Shared papers cannot reuse an occupied seat
Room layouts support visual seating and printing
Published seating changes require a new exam version
notes: The baseline allocator orders eligible students by ID and fills available numbered seats in allocated rooms. Overrides must preserve full student coverage and avoid duplicate seats. Optional AI seating has a separate proposal validator. Do not claim the baseline allocator guarantees anti-cheating separation or globally optimal seating.

title: Invigilation and replacement
body:
Assignment checks availability and overlapping duties
Daily duty limits help constrain workload
Teachers request replacement at least 48 hours early
Eligible reserve staff support replacement proposals
Administrator approval transfers the duty
notes: Candidate selection uses active reserve teachers from the relevant department and filters unavailable or committed staff. The default daily duty limit is two unless teacher settings change it. A request does not release the existing duty. Approval rechecks eligibility and records the replacement. AI may assist candidate selection when configured, while the eligibility checks remain in server code.

title: Admit cards and QR verification
body:
PDF admit cards link students to published exams
Bulk generation can run through a queue worker
QR codes contain a signed verification URL
Verification checks current eligibility and exam status
The public page exposes limited identity information
notes: A UUID identifies the admit record, while Laravel signs the URL to detect URL tampering. Verification requires an active student, eligible profile, published exam, enabled admit issuance and scheduled eligible courses. The page shows name, roll number, exam name and validity, without exposing the full profile. A QR code is not biometric identity proof. Staff must still compare the card to the person.

title: Teacher marks workflow
body:
Enter marks for an authorized course and section
Save a draft or preview a spreadsheet import
Validate score limits, duplicates and student eligibility
Submit only after every component is complete
Submitted marks lock until an administrator returns them
notes: Distinguish three cases: zero is an actual score, absent is an explicit flag with blank score, and missing is incomplete information. Missing marks block submission and calculation. Approved or published result batches lock direct marks editing. Submission deadlines are configurable and displayed, but do not describe them as a strict late-write ban without checking the relevant enforcement.

title: Grading calculation
body:
Weighted percentage = sum of (score ÷ maximum × weight)
Illustration: 16/20 × 20 + 60/80 × 80 = 76%
Approved boundaries determine grade and grade points
Quality points = course credits × grade points
GPA = total quality points ÷ total credits
notes: The example is illustrative, not a student record. Component weights must sum to 100. BCMath decimal operations reduce floating-point inconsistencies. The scheme controls rounding places. Passing compares the percentage with the configured passing-to-maximum ratio. An absent component contributes zero and sets the absence flag. Do not claim absence always forces failure, because the calculation uses the final weighted percentage. Academic GPA uses final-exam results, with configurable latest-attempt handling.

title: Result review and publication
body:
Draft results
Submitted for review
Under review
Approved
Published to students
notes: ResultsService restricts state transitions and checks completeness and expected eligible result counts. Approval recalculates the results so returned and resubmitted marks do not leave stale calculated values. Publication requires the examination schedule to be published. Students only see their own published results. The approval stage is an administrative control, not an external accreditation decision.

title: Corrections and student rechecks
body:
Students request review of their own published result
Administrators record the recheck decision and reason
A recheck approval does not automatically edit marks
Published mark corrections record old and new values
A different administrator approves the correction
notes: Published corrections use a separate record and require an approver different from the requester. The service rejects approval if the underlying mark changed after the proposal. On approval, it recalculates the affected student result and sends a notification. Two active administrator accounts are needed to demonstrate this workflow end to end.

title: AI assistance and statistical analysis
body:
AI can propose schedules, seating and import mappings
Server validators check proposals before approval
The assistant reads authorized records and can explain them
Rule checks flag incomplete data and statistical outliers
Forecasts estimate trends from published final attempts
notes: Do not describe all analysis as generative AI. AnalysisService performs deterministic completeness rules and flags deviation greater than two population standard deviations when the sample meets its checks. Flags request human review and do not establish misconduct. ForecastService uses up to eight published final attempts, a last-observation baseline for fewer than three, and least-squares regression from three onward. It does not change official grades. Provider-backed features require configuration and network access.

title: Security and record integrity
body:
Authentication, active-account checks and role middleware
Policies and scoped queries enforce record access
Validation and state locks protect academic workflows
Transactions and row locks support consistent writes
Audit records preserve important actions and reasons
notes: Passwords use Laravel’s hashed model cast. Laravel web middleware supplies form/session protection. Login and selected endpoints are throttled. Signed URLs protect public admit links. These are implemented controls, not evidence that the system has passed a penetration test. The audit log is stored in the application database and should not be called immutable or tamper-proof. Backups have integrity checks but the ZIP is not shown to be encrypted.

title: Testing and current evidence
body:
Repository includes PHP feature and security tests
Browser scripts cover role workflows and interface behavior
Frontend tests cover countdown and admit QR behavior
Concurrency and queue smoke scripts also exist
This review verified source, not a passing runtime test run
notes: State this clearly: vendor and node_modules are absent from this checkout. No application test run, load benchmark, user study or production reliability result is claimed. Review tests/Feature for workflow, role, import, AI, security, deadlines and admit verification cases. PHP tests require a disposable MySQL database ending in _test and can reset its tables.

title: Contribution and next steps
body:
One connected workflow for the examination lifecycle
Publication gates help prevent incomplete records
Separate approvals support accountable corrections
Optional AI adds assistance to rule-based operations
Next: measured usability, load and recovery testing
notes: Closing: “The main contribution is integrating examination operations with controlled publication and traceable decisions. The code implements these controls. The next evaluation should measure usability and performance using representative institutional data.” Future ideas include stronger schedule optimization, institutional SSO and integration APIs. Present these as proposed work, not delivered features.

title: Live demonstration
body:
1. Administrator: inspect academic setup and a draft exam
2. Demonstrate a conflict and then valid seating and duties
3. Teacher: enter marks, show validation, submit
4. Administrator: calculate, review, approve and publish
5. Student: view result, admit card and recheck request
notes: Reserve about 4–6 minutes if time allows. Rehearse on a separate demo database. Prepare a future exam with eligible enrollments, approved grading, component weights totaling 100%, room capacity and assigned teachers. Keep additional data ready for invalid marks and schedule conflicts. Show the QR verification in a browser. If the live environment fails, use the included screenshots and explain the same workflow. Do not show .env, logs, email reset tokens or API keys.

title: Database relationships
body:
Academic records: sessions, departments, semesters, sections
People: users, student profiles and teacher profiles
Teaching: enrollments and teacher assignments
Exams: examinations, exam courses and components
Operations: schedules, rooms, seats, duties and admit cards
Results: submissions, marks, batches, calculated results
notes: Key relationships: session has semesters, semester and department have sections, user has role profile, student has enrollments, examination has exam_courses, exam_course has components and one schedule, schedule has rooms and seating plan, seating plan has seats, component has student marks, examination has result batch, batch has calculated results. Foreign keys and compound unique constraints enforce relational integrity. Consult the generated schema appendix for the complete migration inventory.

title: Request flow and code organization
body:
routes/web.php selects the endpoint and middleware
Controllers validate requests and authorize actions
Services enforce domain rules inside transactions
Eloquent models read and write MySQL records
Blade views and PDF templates present the result
notes: Example: POST /workflow/marks/{course} passes through authentication and role middleware, calls WorkflowController::marks, authorizes the exam_course, and delegates to MarksService. MarksService checks assignment, batch locks, rows and completeness, then persists the submission and audit event. Resources/js and resources/css contain frontend sources. Public assets are browser-accessible. Private documents belong in storage.

title: Imports and reporting
body:
Student imports use roll number, name, email and section
Marks imports use roll number, component, score and absence
CSV and XLSX paths support validation and preview
Confirmed imports apply domain checks
PDF outputs support admit cards and reports
notes: Baseline CSV headers must exactly match the expected fields, and parsing caps input at 1000 rows. Student imports reject existing emails and roll numbers and use a transaction on commit. Imported students set passwords through recovery rather than receiving a shared default. AI imports are an optional assisted path and should not be confused with ordinary deterministic CSV/XLSX validation.

title: Queues, backups and deployment
body:
Serve Laravel from the public directory
Run a queue worker for background tasks
Run scheduled tasks for backups and reset-token cleanup
Backups include SQL, private files and signed checksums
Restore to a separate empty database ending in _restore
notes: README supports Windows installation with PHP 8.2+, Composer, MySQL and optional frontend builds. Queue and scheduler are separate long-running processes in local setup. Backup runs daily at 02:00 Asia/Karachi when the scheduler operates. HMAC and SHA-256 checks detect archive changes. Keep the original APP_KEY securely. Restore stages data for review without automatically switching the live database. Do not claim encrypted backups or validated recovery time.

title: Limitations and evaluation gaps
body:
Greedy scheduling does not guarantee an optimal timetable
Forecast quality depends on limited comparable history
AI suggestions require validation and human review
No load benchmark or user-study result is established
Live readiness depends on dependencies and infrastructure
notes: Other practical constraints: the baseline import path has a 1000-row cap, workers must run for queued work, and SMTP is needed to deliver email. Local log mail writes email content to a file instead of sending it. Audit logs do not prevent a privileged database operator from changing records. Improvements should follow institutional requirements and measured evaluation.

title: Likely defense questions
body:
Why Laravel and MySQL?
What prevents unauthorized marks changes?
What if scheduling or AI fails?
How do you distinguish zero, absent and missing?
What evidence supports the project’s effectiveness?
notes: Answers: Laravel provides MVC, middleware, policies, ORM, queues and testing support. MySQL fits related academic data and transactional integrity. Marks use assignment checks, locks and controlled corrections. Scheduling rolls back if no feasible slot is found, and manual/rule-based workflows remain available without AI. Zero is a score, absence is explicit and missing blocks completeness. Effectiveness needs measured evaluation. Present existing tests as code coverage intentions until a passing run is recorded.

title: Defense evidence map
body:
Features and access: routes/web.php and policies
Rules: scheduling, marks, grading and results services
Data design: migrations and Eloquent models
AI boundaries: AI services and assistant context
Validation plan: tests and installation guidance
notes: Use this slide to point reviewers to concrete implementation evidence. All statements in this deck describe the checked-out repository. Screenshot data is illustrative. Runtime behavior and operational readiness still need a dependency-complete environment. The companion guide includes slide notes, detailed Q&A, schema inventory and a demo checklist.
